questions.question: If a number is divided by 30 then it leaves 17 as a remainder. What will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 10?
questions.solution:
If a number is divided by 30 then it leaves 17 as a remainder

∴ The number is

= 30n + 17, n is a natural number

= 30n + 10 + 7

= 10(3n + 1) + 7

∴ 7 will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 10

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by 11?
questions.solution:
A number will be divisible by 11 if difference of sum of digits in odd positions and sum of digits in even positions is divisible by 11

For number 59609,

Sum of digits in odd position = 5 + 6 + 9 = 20

Sum of digits in odd position = 9 + 0 = 9

∴ Difference between sum of digits in odd position and sum of digits in even position

= 20 - 9

= 11, which is divisible by 11

∴ 59609 is divisible by 11

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B can do the same piece of work in 30 days. They start working together and work for 5 days and then both leave the work. C alone finishes the remaining work in 14 days. In how many days will C alone finish the whole work?
questions.solution:
A can do a piece of work in 20 days

Part of work A can do in a day = 1/20

B can do a piece of work in 30 days.

Part of work B can do in a day = 1/30

∴ Part of work A and B can do in 5 days together = 5/20 + 5/30 = 25/60 = 5/12

∴ Remaining part of work

= 1 - (5/12)

= 7/12

C finishes 7/12th part of the work in 14 days

∴ C can complete the whole work alone in 14/(7/12) = 24 days

questions.question: P, Q and R undertook a work for Rs. 48000. Together P and Q complete 5/12th part of the work. What is the share (in Rs.) of R?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 1.

As per the question

 P and Q complete the 5/12th part of the total work

∴ Part of work completed by R,

= Total work - (P & Q part of work)

= 1 - (5/12)

= 7/12

The total amount for total work = Rs. 48000

Work is directly proportional to salary,

**∴ Share of R = (7/12) × 48000 = Rs. 28000**

questions.question: The length of two parallel sides of a trapezium are 30 cm and 40 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 350 cm², then what is the value (in cm) of its height?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The lengths of two parallel sides of a trapezium are 30 cm and 40 cm.

Area of the trapezium = 350 cm²

**Formula used:**

Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

where a and b → length of two parallel sides

h → height

**Calculation:**

Area of trapezium = 350

⇒ 1/2 × (30 + 40) × h = 350

⇒ 1/2 × 70 × h = 350

⇒ h = (350 × 2)/70

⇒ h = 10cm

**∴ The height of trapezium = 10cm**

questions.question: If the difference between discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 20% on a certain bill is Rs. 3, then what is the amount (in Rs.) of the bill?
questions.solution:
Let, the amount of bill is Rs. x

When Discount of 35% is applied

Amount of bill

= (1 - 0.35) x

= 0.65x

When two successive discount of 20% is applied

Amount of bill

= (1 - 0.20) (1 - 0.20)x

= 0.80 × 0.80 × x

= 0.64x

The difference between these two amounts is Rs. 3

∴ 0.65x - 0.64x = 3

⇒ 0.01x = 3

⇒ x = 300

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9549a78f1c909762f0e9b9a8ae0bf3da5b964b64141e062c8cb60df8b63db830.png] 

First discount = 35%

Second discount = 2 successive discounts of 20%

We can calculate two successive discounts by 2y – y²/100, here y is discount%

Second discount = 2 × 20 – (20)²/100 = 40 – 4 = 36%

Difference in discount = 36% – 35% = 1%

1% of the bill = Rs 3

⇒ Total bill = 3 × 100/1 = Rs. 300 

**∴ Total bill is Rs. 300**

questions.question: If a shopkeeper marks the price of goods 40% more than their cost price and allows a discount of 40%, then what is his gain or loss percent?
questions.solution:
Let,

The cost price is Rs. x

Marked price is 40% more than cost price

∴ Marked price = Rs. 1.40x

Discount = 40%

∴ Selling price = 0.60 × (1.40x) = 0.84x

∴ Loss% = [(Cost Price - Selling price)/Cost Price] × 100%

= [(x - 0.84x)/x] × 100%

= 0.16 × 100%

= 16%

questions.question: The ratio of two positive numbers is 9 : 11. Their product is 6336. What is the smallest number?
questions.solution:
Let, Two numbers are 9x and 11x

Their product is 6336

∴ (9x) × (11x) = 6336

⇒ 99x² = 6336

⇒ x² = 64

⇒ x = 8

∴ Smallest number is = 9x = 9 × 8 = 72

questions.question: B starts some business by investing Rs. 90000. After 4 months, D joins business by investing Rs. 80000. At the end of the year, in what ratio will they share the profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

B starts some business by investing Rs. 90000.

After 4 months, D joins the business by investing Rs. 80000.

**Formula Used∶**

Basic Knowledge of Ratio

The ratio of shares of partners = Ratio of their investments.

**Calculation∶**

B invest Rs. 90000 for 12 months

D invest Rs. 80000 for 8 months

Ratio of share of profit of B and D

⇒ 90000 × 12 : 80000 × 8

⇒ 9 × 12 : 8 × 8

⇒ 9 × 3 : 2 × 8

⇒ 27 : 16

**∴ At the end of the year, in ratio 27 : 16 will they share the profit.**

questions.question: The average of 9 numbers is 20. If the number 30 is also included, then what will be the average of these 10 numbers?
questions.solution:
The average of 9 numbers is 20.

∴ The sum of these 9 numbers = 20 × 9 = 180

If a number 30 is also included.

The sum of these 10 numbers = 180 + 30 = 210

∴ The average of these 10 numbers = 210/10 = 21

questions.question: By selling 50 metres of cloth, a person gains the cost price of 20 metres of cloth. What is his gain percent?
questions.solution:
Let,

The cost price of 1 metre = Rs. x

Cost price of 20 metre = Rs. 20x

Cost price of 50 metre = Rs. 50x

Given,

By selling 50 metres, he gains the cost price of 20

= Cost price of 50 metre + cost price of 20 metre

= 50x + 20x

= 70x

∴ Profit percent = [(Selling price of 50 metres - cost price of 50 metres)/Cost Price of 50 metres] × 100%

= [(70x - 50x)/50x] × 100%

= (2/5) × 100

= 40%

questions.question: If some articles are bought at Rs. 10 each and sold at Rs. 7 each, then what is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The cost price of one article = Rs. 10

The selling price of the article = Rs 7

**Formula used:**

Loss = CP - SP

Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100

Here, SP → Selling price, CP → Cost price

**Calculation:**

Loss = 10 - 7 = 3

Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100

⇒ (3/10) × 100

⇒ 30%

**∴ The loss percentage is 30%**

questions.question: A man saves 30% of his income in 1 year. If he wants to save the same amount in 8 months, then by how much percentage should he increase his monthly savings?
questions.solution:
Let,

Monthly salary of the man = Rs. x

Annual salary of the man = Rs. 12x

He saves 30% of his income

∴ Amount of saving in a month = 0.3x

∴ Amount of savings in a year = Rs. (0.30 × 12x) = Rs. 3.6x

Salary of 8 months = Rs. 8x

Now,

3.6x = 0.45 × 8x = 0.45 of Salary of 8 month

∴ He has to save 45% per month to save Rs. 3.6x in 8 month

New amount of saving in a month = 0.45x

∴ Percentage increase of monthly saving = [(0.45x - 0.30x)/0.30x] × 100% = ½ × 100% = 50%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Let the saved amount be Rs. 24(LCM of 12 and 8)

Now he saves 24 in one year i.e. 12 months, 

⇒ Monthly saving = 24/12 = Rs. 2 per month

In the new scenario, he wants to save Rs. 24 in 8 months

Monthly savings now, 

⇒ 24/8 = Rs 3 per month 

Percent increase in Saving = (3 - 2)/2 × 100

⇒ 1/2 × 100 = 50%

**∴ The percentage increase will be 50%.**

questions.question: A man spends 80% of his income and saves the rest. If his income and spending both increases by 10%, then what is the percentage change in his savings?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If Income and Expenditure both increase by the same percentage (x%), then Savings will also increase by the same percentage (x%).

Given increase in Income = 10%

Given increase in Expenditure = 10%

Since both parts of the income equation increase by 10%, the balancing part (Savings) must also change by 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Income = 100%, Expenditure = 80%, Income & Spending increase = 10%.

**Formula Used:** Income = Expenditure + Savings; % Change = (Change ÷ Original) × 100

 Initial State Exp: 80 Sav: 20 New State (+10%) Exp: 88 Sav: 22 
• Savings: 20 → 22 (10% Increase) 

⇒ Let Initial Income = 100

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 80% of 100 = 80

⇒ Initial Savings = 100 − 80 = 20

⇒ New Income = 100 + (10% of 100) = 110

⇒ New Expenditure = 80 + (10% of 80) = 88

⇒ New Savings = 110 − 88 = 22

⇒ Increase in Savings = 22 − 20 = 2

⇒ % Change in Savings = (2 ÷ 20) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in one part must be balanced by others to maintain the equality.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. This determines the relative growth or decline.

Weighted Average Concept

If income changes by I%, expenditure by E%, and savings by S%, then Income × I% = Expenditure × E% + Savings × S%.

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 25 m/s for 8 hours. What is the distance (in km) travelled by the car?
questions.solution:
Given,

Speed = 25 m/s

Time of journey = 8 hours = 8 × 60 × 60 seconds = 28800 seconds

∴ Distance travelled

= Speed × Time

= (25 × 28800) m

= 720000 m

∵ 1000 m = 1 km

= 720 km

questions.question: A 450 meter long train crosses a bridge 650 meters long in 36 seconds. What is speed (in km/hr) of the train?
questions.solution:
Length of train = 450 m

Length of bridge = 650 m

To cross a bridge train has to cover a distance which is sum of the length of the train and length of the bridge.

∴ Distance covered to cross the bridge

= 450 m + 650 m

= 1100 m

Time required = 36 seconds

∴ Speed = Distance covered/Required time = 1100/36 = (1100/1000)/(36/3600)

= 110 km/hr

questions.question: The population of a town increases at the rate of 15% per annum. If the present population is 108445 of town, then what was the population 2 years ago?
questions.solution:
Let,

The population 2 years ago = x

Increase rate of population = 15%

∴ Population after 1 year = 1.15x

Population after 2 year = 1.15 × 1.15x = 1.3225x

Given,

After 2 year population is = 108445

∴ 1.3225x = 108445

⇒ x = 82000
